conclusion: The bounded OpenAlex citation review surfaced method-level connectome dynamics comparators including: Liew et al. arXiv:2609.01330v1, an optic-lobe visual conductance-LIF model without in-vivo validation; Betzel et al. DOI 10.1371/journal.pcsy.0000091, an adult Drosophila FlyWire v783 stochastic sensory-cascade model; Beirán and Litwin-Kumar DOI 10.1038/s41593-025-02080-4, a teacher-student recurrent-network theory tested against empirical connectome examples; and Pugliese et al. DOI 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944 (canonical S740), dynamic Drosophila VNC simulations for walking CPG hypotheses; plus Walker et al. DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-89088-9, taste-circuit activity simulations. Beirán et al. is canonical S743. S740 and S743 were already canonical; Walker is newly catalogued as S808 and is a distinct publication. Pugliese versions share one DOI and are not two publications. Their model classes and endpoints differ; none establishes nociception, pain, ECAP, SCS, or cross-domain clinical transfer. The separate Calle-Schuler eLife lead remains circuit/behavior prior art without fitted dynamics. PA-01 remains open: the sampled citation/index and targeted query coverage do not complete NS-01-NS-04 exact/synonym/author searches, full backward/forward snowballing, or saturation; all 86/86 indexed S775 citing records in the captured OpenAlex snapshot now have bounded dispositions; global citation coverage and PA-01 saturation remain open. On 2026-09-27 the exact-title/synonym pass also located a new bioRxiv v1 NeuroGraphBench connectome-grounded looming escape circuit model (DOI 10.64898/2026.08.22.746456). It is in-silico NS-04 prior art, not an in-vivo validation or whole-brain nociception model; PA-01 saturation remains unearned and any two-refresh sequence restarts after this new class.
